claims.claim: ⚠️ **In a child with suspected food allergy, nothing matters more than recognising and managing anaphylaxis.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IgE-mediated reactions usually start within 60 minutes of ingestion.** Commonest foods: egg, milk, peanut, tree nuts, fish, shellfish, wheat, soy, sesame.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Anaphylaxis = any acute respiratory and/or cardiovascular symptoms, even without skin signs.** Mild-to-moderate reactions involve only skin and/or gut.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Respiratory:** hoarse voice, throat tightness, difficulty swallowing, stridor, wheeze, persistent cough. **Cardiovascular:** pallor, dizziness, collapse.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk factors:** personal atopy (asthma, eczema, allergic rhinitis) · a parent or sibling with atopy or food allergy · other IgE-mediated food allergies.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A contact reaction around the mouth is common in eczema and is not diagnostic** of IgE-mediated allergy; nor is eczema alone.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **FPIES is non-IgE:** profuse vomiting ± diarrhoea two to four hours after a recently introduced food, sometimes with pallor, poor tone, hypothermia and low blood pressure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not test in the acute setting.** Diagnosis needs a convincing history, supported by skin prick testing or specific IgE done after the event.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Skin prick testing is preferred, by a paediatric allergy-trained clinician only**; otherwise targeted serum specific IgE for the suspected trigger(s) only.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No screening panels and no testing for foods not yet eaten** — they drive unnecessary avoidance and more future allergy. **No allergy testing for non-IgE allergy** (non-IgE cow's milk allergy, FPIES).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Anaphylaxis: give IM adrenaline straight away — 0.01 mL/kg of 1:1000 (10 microgram/kg), max 0.5 mL; if no improvement, repeat at 5 minutes.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mild-to-moderate: non-sedating antihistamine, e.g. cetirizine orally** — 1–2 years 2.5 mg · 2–6 years 5 mg · 6 years and above 10 mg; safe from 6 months at 0.25 mg/kg/dose.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Or loratadine orally once daily:** 1–2 years 2.5 mg · over 2 years and under 30 kg 5 mg · over 30 kg 10 mg.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Observe until symptoms are not escalating**, then discharge with a plan.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A child must avoid the suspected food, but not similar foods already tolerated.** Teach label reading.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tree nuts travel in pairs:** walnut ↔ pecan, cashew ↔ pistachio — avoid both.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give an ASCIA action plan even before the food is confirmed:** red (anaphylaxis) plan after a severe reaction, green (allergy) plan after a mild-to-moderate one.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep a varied diet, including previously tolerated allergenic foods, eaten regularly.** Refer to a dietitian if many or staple foods are being cut.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss with the paediatric or allergy team:** any suspected or proven food anaphylaxis · suspected allergy with unstable asthma · unclear trigger or equivocal tests · multiple food allergies · suspected tolerance that may need an oral food challenge.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Adrenaline auto-injectors** (usually a 12-month expiry; GP can re-prescribe): **150 mcg under 20 kg · 300 mcg from 20 kg · 300–500 mcg close to or above 50 kg.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Find and treat asthma: fatal anaphylaxis is more likely when asthma is poorly controlled.** Re-check action-plan knowledge and auto-injector technique regularly.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Food allergy - IgE mediated food allergy' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Food_allergy_-_IgE_mediated_food_allergy/, retrieved 2026-09-23
